salient_findings: Pulsatile mass in the epigastric region
key_facts: 84-year-old man
Medical history of hyperlipidemia, hypertension, hypothyroidism, and tobacco use
20-pack-year smoking history
Smoking pipe tobacco for the past 10 years
Asymptomatic abdominal mass with pulsations
Vital signs: Temperature - afebrile, Blood pressure - 120/76 mm Hg, Pulse rate - 73 beats/min, Respiratory rate - 16/minute
Pulses were palpable in the lower extremities bilaterally
Complete blood count and electrolyte levels were within normal limits
Computed tomographic angiogram (CTA) of abdomen and pelvis showed a saccular aneurysm
Aneurysmal neck angulation greater than 60 degrees with neck tortuosity noted
Dense calcifications of iliac vessels present without narrowing
No signs of impending rupture

shortlist.label: Abdominal aortic aneurysm
shortlist.why_kept: Large pulsatile mass in epigastric region with soft bruit and significant aneurysm on CTA

shortlist.label: Iliac artery aneurysm
shortlist.why_kept: Dense calcifications of iliac vessels and aneurysmal neck angulation greater than 60 degrees

shortlist.label: Common iliac artery aneurysm
shortlist.why_kept: CTA showed a saccular aneurysm with significant displacement of the right ureter

shortlist.label: Internal iliac artery aneurysm
shortlist.why_kept: Possible involvement of iliac vessels given the patient's smoking history and aneurysm location

shortlist.label: External iliac artery aneurysm
shortlist.why_kept: Less likely but still plausible given the aneurysm's location and patient's risk factors

raw.rationale: The patient's computed tomographic angiogram (CTA) of abdomen and pelvis showed a saccular aneurysm measuring 14.6 cm × 12.6 cm in greatest transaxial dimension, which is consistent with an abdominal aortic aneurysm. The aneurysm's location and size, as well as the presence of dense calcifications of iliac vessels, support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Iliac artery aneurysm
rejected.why: While iliac artery aneurysms can occur, the size and location of the aneurysm in this case are more consistent with an abdominal aortic aneurysm.

rejected.label: Common iliac artery aneurysm
rejected.why: The aneurysm's size and location are not typical for a common iliac artery aneurysm, which is usually smaller and more distal.

rejected.label: Internal iliac artery aneurysm
rejected.why: Internal iliac artery aneurysms are rare and usually present with different symptoms, such as pelvic pain or neurological deficits.

rejected.label: External iliac artery aneurysm
rejected.why: External iliac artery aneurysms are also rare and typically smaller than the aneurysm described in this case.
